title: Eighth Constable's History (Español)
full_text:
The Eighth Constable related:

'Two camel drovers disputed the ownership of a stray camel. I had not seen the beast, but after examining the grazing trail, I declared: "The camel is blind in the left eye, lame in the right hind leg, and carries a load of honey on one side and grain on the other!"

The citizens were astounded, accusing me of having stolen the camel!

I laughed and explained: "The bushes were cropped only on the right side of the trail, proving the beast was blind in the left eye; one hoof made a dragged print, proving lameness; on one side of the trail flies swarmed over dripped honey, and on the other ants carried grain!"

The camel was found exactly as described, proving that sharp deduction from nature’s clues speaks with the certainty of an eyewitness.'
moral: Sharp deduction from environmental signs reconstructs truth without seeing the event. [ES]
